Clarification required I couldn't produce an implementation-ready plan, because the branch this issue targets doesn't contain the code that failed. The plan below is written against `main`, and the last question asks you to confirm a retarget. **Planning ref:** `git rev-parse HEAD` = `1606490e0d46b5a441910504166cadd727d04c04`, symbolic branch `ai/issue-6529`. Integration branch metadata is `ai/issue-6529`, so there is no integration-branch mismatch. ## Conflict detection (blocking) The failing code is not on the target branch `ai/issue-6529`. I checked: - No `scripts/` file on this branch contains `sandbox_path_unsupported` or a `check-paths` subcommand. The resolver failure string ("Conflict resolver isolation unavailable … refusing host fallback") doesn't exist here. - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` is 3,041 lines. Its model call runs on the host: it calls `opencode_run_cmd` directly (around lines 2297-2344) with only a private `GIT_INDEX_FILE` copy (`_resolver_model_index_prepare`, line 553). It has no sandbox preflight. - `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:44` admits `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`. The diagnosis cites an exclusion at lines 60-62, which doesn't exist on this branch. That file's only subcommands here are snapshot / transfer / refresh / readme. - `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py` does not exist on this branch. - The commit the failed run used, `ec4d60e4a9b365a949415a98d799ab7229383aad` (`main`), can't be reached from this checkout. As `agents.md` says, review runs the helpers from the verified workflow commit (`main` here), not from the PR head. Any change on `ai/issue-6529` would edit code paths the failing run never executes, and it could not fix PR #6538 until it reached `main`. The heal intake routed this issue to the PR head branch on the assumption that "that run executed the PR's own workflow code". For this run that assumption was wrong. That's a separate routing defect, outside this issue's scope. The plan below is therefore written against `main`'s sandbox-only resolver, using the line references from the heal diagnosis. The implementer must re-read those regions at implementation time, since this run could not read them. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends the deterministic manifest union-merge block in `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` and the existing `check-paths` sandbox preflight in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers set the scope: Q1=A (narrow paired-hook derivation, live hook stays excluded from the sandbox), Q2=A (log rejected path names alongside the existing error) and Q3=A (handle the manifest delete/modify shape inside the existing resolver). Two existing blocks already do the matching jobs: the manifest union-merge block resolves a generated file on the host without the model, and `check-paths` decides what may enter the sandbox. The paired-hook path is an additive sibling of the manifest block and only shrinks the input `check-paths` sees. Nothing is admitted to the sandbox that wasn't before. A paired path that deliberately leaves the template out was rejected: it adds no meaningful code and would leave the shipped template and the live hook out of step. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the full byte-parity check is required. ## Q1 (live merged-PR guard hook): option A. Q2 (log rejected path names): option A. Q3 (manifest delete/modify shape): option A. **Q3 confirmation.** The manifest block in this branch's `review_conflict_prepare.sh` (around lines 226-229 and 297-299) says delete/modify shapes "fall through to the Codex resolver". On `main` that resolver is sandbox-only and `.ai/` is in `EXCLUDED`. So a delete/modify conflict on `.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt` always ends in `sandbox_path_unsupported`. That is a real unhandled shape, so it is in scope. ## 1. Files likely to change (on `main`) - `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` - New paired-hook detection block, placed after the manifest union-merge block and before the empty-allowlist check. - Extended manifest block for delete/modify. - The `CONFLICTED_PATHS_FILE` capture writes a sibling list of paths the host derives. - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` - The `check-paths` preflight is fed the conflicted paths minus the paths the host derives. - Additive `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_PATH_REJECTED` lines. - A host-side derivation step after the sandbox transfer and before the existing staging, unmerged-entry and commit gates. - `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py`: regression tests (on `main`, this file is expected to exist). - `agents.md`: add `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_PATH_REJECTED` and `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVED` to the stable log-prefix list and the matching `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines. Add one sentence to the Integration-sync section describing the paired derivation. - `changelog.d/-conflict-resolver-paired-hook.md`: changelog fragment (CLAUDE.md §20). Do not change: - `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`: its admission rule stays as it is. - Any `.claude/**` file. - Any workflow YAML. ## 2. Functions and modules to implement **A. Paired-hook detection** (`review_conflict_prepare.sh`) - Constants: - `PAIRED_HOOK_LIVE_PATH=".claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py"` - `PAIRED_HOOK_TWIN_PATH="workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py"` - Kill switch `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVE_ENABLED`, default `true`. This name is unique in this tree; re-grep on `main`. - Eligibility. All of the following must hold: - Both paths appear in `git ls-files -u`. - For each of stages 1, 2 and 3, the stage is present for both paths or absent for both, with identical blob OID and identical mode (compare the `git ls-files -u -s` columns). - Stages 2 and 3 are both present, so it's a content conflict. - Neither path, nor any of its parent directories, is a symlink in the worktree. - When eligible: - Remove the live path from `RESOLVER_ALLOWLIST_FILE`, so the model prompt and the sandbox snapshot never include it. - Write `PAIRED_HOOK_LIVE_PATHPAIRED_HOOK_TWIN_PATH` to `${RUNTIME_DIR}/paired_hook_derivations.tsv`. - Keep the live path in `conflicted_paths.txt`. `check_resolver_diff.sh`'s touched ⊆ conflicted guard must still allow the host to write it. - Log `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVED phase=prepare live=

twin=

`. - In every other case nothing changes, and the live path still fails closed in the preflight. **B. Preflight input filter and rejection logging** (`review_conflict_resolve.sh`, around the `check-paths` call, cited lines 2239-2247) - Build the input list for `check-paths` as `conflicted_paths.txt` minus the live paths in `paired_hook_derivations.tsv`. Only an exact path match for a row written by A is removed. - On rejection, run `check-paths` once per path (or use a rejected-name list, if the `main` version prints one) to find which paths were rejected. - For each rejected path, emit `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_PATH_REJECTED path=`. - Sanitize with `printf '%s' "$p" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_./@+-' '_' | cut -c1-200`. This removes newlines, `::` command injection and percent-encoding tricks. - Cap the output at 50 lines. - Keep the existing `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK … reason=sandbox_path_unsupported` line, the `::error::` text and the fail-closed exit byte for byte as they are. **C. Host derivation** (`review_conflict_resolve.sh`) - Runs after a successful sandbox resolution and transfer, before the existing staging of resolved paths and the unmerged-entry and `[ai-merge-resolve]` commit gates. - For each row in `paired_hook_derivations.tsv`: 1. The twin must be a regular, non-symlink file with no conflict marker lines (`^(<<<<<<< |=======$|>>>>>>> )`). 2. Re-check that the live path and its parent directories are not symlinks. 3. Write the twin's bytes atomically to the live path: temp file in the same directory, then `mv`. Apply the recorded mode. 4. `git add -- `. 5. Check `cmp -s` on the worktree files and that `git ls-files -s` shows the same OID and mode for both paths. 6. Log `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVED phase=resolve outcome=staged`. - Any failure logs `::error::` plus `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVED … outcome=failed reason=` and fails the resolver. There is no fallback to host model resolution. - The existing validation (unmerged-entry check, `check_resolver_diff.sh`, fingerprints) then runs unchanged. - If the run short-circuits with `CONFLICT_RESOLVED=true` (only the manifest conflicted), the TSV is empty. A only writes rows when the live hook is unmerged, so a short-circuit can't leave a pending derivation. Assert that at the short-circuit point. **D. Manifest delete/modify** (`review_conflict_prepare.sh`, the manifest block's `case` statement) - New arm for "stage 1 present and exactly one of stage 2 or stage 3 present" (the modify side survives). - Resolve to the surviving side's blob: `git show ::path` written through the same `LC_ALL=C sort -u` normalisation, then `git add`. - Why the surviving side: the manifest is a regenerable inventory that `workspace_init.sh` rewrites. Keeping the surviving content is the conservative, data-preserving choice. - Log `Manifest union-merge: resolved delete/modify (kept stage )`. - Shapes with only stage 1, or other unknown shapes, keep the existing fall-through log. - Reuse the existing "only conflict → commit now" tail unchanged. ## 3. Data structures affected - New runtime file `${RUNTIME_DIR}/paired_hook_derivations.tsv` (one row per pair, three columns). It is never committed or uploaded. - `conflicted_paths.txt` keeps the same meaning. `RESOLVER_ALLOWLIST_FILE` loses the derived live path. - No change to Git, issue, label or state schemas. ## 4. API and interface changes - New env var `CONFLICT_PAIRED_HOOK_DERIVE_ENABLED`, default `tru
